target_customer: SMEs and e-commerce businesses in Saudi Arabia and the UAE needing working capital
problem: Regional SMEs struggle to get bank credit. erad uses sales, marketing and banking data to give Shariah-compliant financing offers within 48 hours.
business_model: Lending: revenue-based and fixed-term Shariah-compliant financing funded by equity and debt facilities, earning financing fees
product_category: SME working capital and non-dilutive growth financing

founders.name: Salem Abu-Hammour
previous_startups: Online coffee e-commerce store co-launched with Faris Yaghmour (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he previously worked in M&A and banking.

founders.name: Faris Yaghmour
previous_startups: Online coffee e-commerce store co-launched with Salem Abu-Hammour (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page says 4 years in retail and corporate banking product and operations. Wamda quotes him saying the idea came from his own struggle to finance an e-commerce business.

founders.name: Youssef Said
founders.background_notes: YC page says 10 years in tech consulting and product engineering in Europe, then large e-commerce programs in the Middle East.

founders.name: Abdulmalik Almeheini
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the Wamda 2025 and 2026 articles; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: FlapKap
competitors.what: Revenue-based financing for e-commerce and SaaS businesses in MENA, based in Egypt and expanding to the UAE and Saudi Arabia
competitors.funding_then: $1.2M in March 2022 and $3.6M seed announced October 2022 led by QED, Nclude, Outliers and A15

technical_complexity.rationale: Data connections to sales, marketing and banking sources plus credit models and Shariah compliant structuring are standard fintech engineering. Funding the loan book is the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: Licensing, lender relationships and repayment data compound over time, but others can copy revenue based financing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found in sources. erad raised a pre-Series A in 2025 and a Series A in September 2026.

market_need_then: Wamda 2025 cites an estimated $250 billion SME credit gap in the region and says over 60 percent of erad customers were first time credit takers. Founders cite their own difficulty financing an e-commerce business.

branding.domain_note: Uses erad.co; redirects to ksa.erad.co. History not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Offer within 48 hours, data and insight focused

brand_strength.rationale: Brand search found no coverage of the name or identity. Press covers funding and traction, not the brand.

outcome_analysis: erad grew from a $2.4M pre-seed in September 2022 to a $16M round in April 2025, a $33M debt facility in September 2025, a reported $125M Jefferies led facility in November 2025 and a $22M Series A in September 2026, with claimed 8x growth in Saudi Arabia. It benefited from a large SME credit gap and founders with banking and e-commerce experience.
notes: The April 2025 round was called pre-Series A by the press, so stage is 'other'. The $125M Jefferies facility is from Wamda's 2026 article only. The $33M debt round date comes from a Sep 2025 article update with a Wamda-style cross report (Sharikat Mubasher). The Wamda 2026 article is a single outlet for the Series A. Competitor FlapKap source is dated October 2022, a few weeks after the batch. Founder education not found.
